transcript.content: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. To get us started, could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Well, my regular doctor actually sent me. She says I've gotten too thin. 

I mean, I guess I can see it—my work pants are hanging pretty loose on me these days when I'm on my shift. But... I don't know, to be honest, part of me still feels relieved when I step on the scale and the number is lower. So she wanted me to come talk to you about it.
Do you ever feel that you lose control over your eating and end up consuming an unusually large amount of food in a short period of time?

No, I don't have that problem. I actually keep pretty tight control over what I eat. I've never really sat down and eaten a huge amount of food all at once, or felt like I couldn't stop. If anything, it's more the opposite for me.
Since you keep such tight control over your eating, do you ever engage in behaviors like self-induced vomiting or the use of laxatives to help manage your weight?

No, I don't do anything like that. I've never made myself throw up, and I don't take laxatives. Like I said, I just keep a really tight lid on what I eat in the first place, so... I don't feel the need to do those other things.
How would you describe your body shape and weight when you look at yourself in the mirror?

Well, it's... I guess it's tied to how I feel about myself. When I look in the mirror and I look small and neat, I feel like I'm handling everything right, you know? Like I've got things under control. But if I see my stomach looking even the least bit full or round... I just feel like I've completely let myself go. It bothers me a lot.
Have you noticed any changes in your menstrual cycle since you've lost weight?
Well, I'm 64, so... I haven't had a menstrual cycle in a long time. I went through menopause years ago, way before I started losing this weight. So, no, there haven't been any changes like that.
